thread:
alex: Quick heads-up — I opened a PR to consolidate guidance on handling backpressure (rate limits, 429s, timeouts, and context-limit fallbacks). Focus is: readable troubleshooting steps + small SDK snippets for streaming + graceful fallback. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/342
maria: Nice, thanks. Can you add an explicit example for when a streaming call times out and we fallback to a shorter model? That's a frequent ask from customers. :eyes:
sam: I can write that snippet. Thinking of showing a pattern with a short timeout, catching the timeout, then reissuing to a smaller model and copying partial chat/history. Something like:
```python
try:
    with client.chat.stream(model="redwood-13b", timeout=2.5) as stream:
        for token in stream:
            print(token, end="")
except TimeoutError:
    # fallback to smaller model synchronously
    resp = client.chat.complete(model="redwood-7b", messages=history)
    print(resp.text)
```
Keep it simple for the docs, mention tradeoffs.
alex: Perfect — add a short note about token accounting when we reissue (prefix tokens + history). Also mention possible double-charge and how to mitigate with idempotency keys or server-side prefix caching.
kevin: Also we should include the CLI/curl example for ops teams that hit 429s in infra testing. Eg:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"...","timeout":1.5}'
# If you get 429, try: reduce batch size / use model variant with lower memory / add exponential backoff header
```
docs-bot: link-checker: PR #342 — 1 broken link found: docs/examples/old-backoff.md -> 404.
maria: Ah, that's the old backoff doc — remove reference and point to new migration guide (docs/migration/retry-patterns.md).
sam: I'll update the PR. Also adding a short migration note for SDK v2 param rename: old `context_length` -> new `context_limit`. Show tiny mapping table and an example snippet for trimming history before send.
alex: Good call. Include a tiny utility example for trimming by tokens (pseudo-code OK):
```python
def trim_history(history, max_tokens):
    # naive from the end until under budget
    while count_tokens(history) > max_tokens:
        history.pop(0)
    return history
```
kevin: Can we also add a one-line note about fallback ordering: try local quantized variant -> smaller dense model -> queued async job. That helps platform teams pick a policy.
maria: +1. Also mark the troubleshooting page as "operational guidance" so customers know it's prescriptive.
sam: Updated the PR with the snippets, fixed the broken link, and added a short checklist for what to include in a support ticket (logs, request-id, model, latency histogram). PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/342/files
docs-bot: CI: docs build succeeded, link-check passed.
alex: Awesome — can someone review the wording around "possible double-charge". We need it accurate but not scary. Maybe say: "optional mitigation: idempotency keys and prefix caching to avoid duplicate billed completions".
kevin: I'll do a quick copyedit. Expect comments in the PR. :thumbsup:
alex: Thanks all — plan to merge after Kevin's copyedit and one more SRE quick glance. If anyone sees missing coverage (e.g., embeddings rate limits) flag it and I'll add a short section.
maria: I'll skim for embeddings edge-cases tomorrow AM. Good job converging.
